title: McDonald’s Corporation (MCD): One of the Best Low Risk High Growth Stocks to Buy
content:
We just covered the 14 Best Low Risk High Growth Stocks to Buy Right Now and McDonald’s Corporation (NYSE:MCD) ranks 14th on this list.

McDonald’s Corporation (NYSE:MCD) is a 70-year-old brand. It has recently transformed into a data-driven real estate and AI powerhouse, shifting its growth trajectory. The smart money has been pouring into the company because unlike most fast-food chains, McDonald’s is primarily a real estate company. It owns the land under 85% of its restaurants. It leases this land back to franchisees, ensuring a stable, high-margin rent stream that is largely independent of whether a specific store has a bad month in sales. In 2025, the company generated $7.2 billion in free cash flow. This massive liquidity allows it to weather economic downturns, as consumers trade down to McDonald’s value meals when luxury dining becomes too expensive.

title: SoundHound AI: Could the Stock 10X by 2030?
content:
SoundHound AI(NASDAQ: SOUN), a developer of speech and audio recognition services, went public through a merger with a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) four years ago. Its stock started trading at $8.72, but it's trading below $8 as of this writing.

Could this out-of-favor AI stock bounce back and generate a ten-bagger return by 2030? Let's review its business model, growth rates, and valuations to see where its stock is headed.

Will AI create the world's first trillionaire? Our team just released a report on the one little-known company, called an "Indispensable Monopoly" providing the critical technology Nvidia and Intel both need. Continue »Image source: Getty Images.

What does SoundHound do?

SoundHound's namesake app can identify songs by hearing just a few seconds of recorded audio or a few hummed bars. However, most of its revenue and growth comes from Houndify, its developer platform for creating customized AI-powered voice recognition services. It's a popular choice for restaurants, automakers, retailers, and other companies that want to build their own voice-activated services without sharing their data with a tech giant like Microsoft or Alphabet's Google.

After going public, SoundHound expanded its ecosystem by acquiring the AI restaurant services provider SYNQ3, the online food ordering platform Allset, the conversational AI company Amelia, and the customer service AI company Interactions. It also recently agreed to buy LivePerson, a developer of conversation AI tools for companies. All of those acquisitions increased its exposure to the restaurant sector and the growing AI chatbot market.

From 2022 to 2025, SoundHound's revenue rose more than fivefold, from $31 million to $169 million. Yet much of that expansion was fueled by acquisitions rather than organic growth in its core business. The integration of those lower-margin businesses, along with intense competition from bigger companies, reduced its gross margin from 69% in 2022 to 42% in 2025.

On the bright side, SoundHound's adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) improved from negative $73 million in 2022 to negative $58 million in 2025. It's trying to narrow those losses by streamlining its cloud infrastructure costs (especially across its acquired companies), replacing third-party software with its own in-house software, and increasing its mix of higher-margin subscription and royalty-based revenues.

Could SoundHound AI generate a ten-bagger gain by 2030?

From 2025 to 2028, analysts expect SoundHound AI's revenue to grow at 16% CAGR to $265 million, while its adjusted EBITDA turns positive in the final two years. That's a decent growth rate, but it would represent a significant deceleration from its previous years.

Story Continues

Much of SoundHound's early growth was driven by big enterprise contracts, which generate uneven revenues, and acquisitions, which only provide temporary gains. As it gains fewer enterprise customers and acquires fewer companies, its growth will cool off.

It's trying to expand into a "one-stop shop" for agentic AI solutions, but that expansion will require it to increase its headcount and ramp up its data center spending. That pressure will make it harder to stabilize its margins and narrow its losses. Those issues could cause it to underperform its AI peers as more investors focus on profits instead of breakneck sales growth.

The messy macro headwinds will also drive investors away from pricier, more speculative AI stocks. With a market cap of $3.3 billion, SoundHound doesn't seem like a bargain at 14 times this year's sales. It's also more than doubled its share count since its public debut, and its insiders haven't bought a single share over the past three months.

If SoundHound matches analysts' estimates, grows its revenue at a 15% CAGR from 2028 to 2030, and trades at a more modest 10 times sales, its market cap would only rise 6% to $3.5 billion over the next five years. But if it trades at a more generous 15 times sales, its market cap would increase about 60% to $5.3 billion. Either way, SoundHound probably won't come anywhere close to delivering a ten-bagger gain by the beginning of the next decade.

title: SoundHound vs. Cerence: Which Voice AI Stock Has Stronger Potential?
content:
Voice artificial intelligence is becoming one of the most important software themes in 2026 as automakers, restaurants, enterprises and digital platforms look to improve customer engagement, automate workflows and create smarter user experiences. Two notable public companies in this space are SoundHound AI SOUN and Cerence CRNC, both of which specialize in conversational AI and voice-enabled solutions.

While both companies operate in voice AI, their business models differ. SoundHound is expanding across automotive, restaurants, customer service and enterprise automation, while Cerence has historically been strongest in automotive voice assistants and connected car software. Both are now pushing deeper into generative AI and agentic AI, making the comparison timely for investors.

Each stock has pulled back sharply year to date, but both have rebounded strongly over the past month. Investors may be wondering which offers the better risk-reward setup now. Let’s dive deep and closely compare the fundamentals of the two stocks to determine which one is a better investment now.

The Case for SoundHound Stock

SoundHound has emerged as one of the more aggressive growth stories in AI software. The company reported 2025 revenue of $168.9 million, up 99% year over year, while fourth-quarter revenue climbed 59% to $55.1 million. Management said it closed a record number of enterprise deals in the quarter, highlighting strong demand across multiple verticals.

What makes SoundHound compelling is diversification. The company is no longer just an automotive voice platform. It is winning business in restaurants, telecom, healthcare, retail, financial services and hospitality. It also continues expanding in auto with wins in Japan, Korea, Europe and other global markets. That broad reach reduces dependence on any one industry.

Another key catalyst is the planned LivePerson acquisition. Management expects the combined business to create a $500 million revenue opportunity, expand enterprise relationships and strengthen its omnichannel presence across voice, messaging and digital customer interactions. If integrated well, the deal could materially scale SoundHound’s enterprise platform.

SoundHound also benefits from being viewed as an AI-native company rather than a legacy software provider trying to adapt. That positioning could help it win customers seeking next-generation automation solutions.

However, risks remain. SoundHound is still unprofitable on a non-GAAP basis, and investors are paying a premium for future growth execution.

Story Continues

The Case for Cerence Stock

Cerence offers a different investment profile. It is more established in automotive voice AI, with technology embedded in more than 525 million vehicles shipped globally. That scale, deep OEM relationships and domain expertise provide a meaningful competitive moat in the auto industry.

The company delivered strong fiscal first-quarter 2026 results. Revenue increased to $115.1 million from $50.9 million a year ago, while adjusted EBITDA reached $44.6 million. Free cash flow of $35.6 million marked a quarterly record, reflecting improving execution and cost discipline.

Cerence is also advancing its next-generation Cerence xUI platform, which integrates LLM-powered experiences for automakers. Management said it now has five significant xUI programs underway, with first production vehicles expected in 2026. The company recently expanded with BYD, one of the world’s leading EV makers, further validating demand for its technology.

Unlike SoundHound, Cerence is already showing stronger profitability and cash generation. That can be attractive in a market where investors increasingly reward disciplined AI companies rather than pure growth names.

Still, Cerence has challenges. Its business remains heavily tied to auto production cycles, OEM budgets and vehicle launch timing. Revenue can be lumpy due to licensing deals and patent settlements. In fact, a meaningful portion of the first-quarter revenue came from a one-time $49.5 million Samsung patent license payment, which may not repeat.

Market Momentum Tells an Interesting Story

Both stocks have struggled in 2026, but recent momentum has improved. SOUN shares are down 17.5% year to date, while CRNC has plunged 19.2%. Both have underperformed the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector but outperformed their Zacks Computers - IT Services industry benchmark on a relative basis.

In the past month, however, SOUN surged 29.3%, and CRNC rose 29.6%, showing renewed investor appetite for voice AI names. Cerence’s rebound likely reflects improving profitability and automotive wins, while SoundHound’s move appears tied to growth momentum and the LivePerson deal.

SOUN & CRNC 1-Month Share Price PerformanceZacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Valuation Gap Is Massive

The valuation contrast is stark. SoundHound trades at 14.09X forward sales, above the industry’s 12.44X multiple. Cerence trades at just 1.21X forward sales.

That discount suggests Cerence offers far more value on current fundamentals, while SoundHound reflects a premium growth multiple. For investors seeking cheaper AI exposure, Cerence stands out. For investors seeking high-growth optionality, SoundHound may justify its premium.

SOUN vs CRNC ValuationZacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Estimate Revisions Favor Cerence

The Zacks Consensus Estimate trends currently favor Cerence. CRNC’s 2026 EPS estimate improved to 71 cents from 70 cents over the past 60 days, indicating stabilizing sentiment. The consensus estimate also calls for 2026 EPS to decline 6.6% year over year, despite revenue growth of 26.2%, suggesting margin or mix pressures.

For CRNC StockZacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

By contrast, SoundHound’s expected 2026 loss widened to 9 cents from 6 cents. While revenue is projected to grow a stronger 37.8%, the estimate revision signals investors may need to wait longer for earnings leverage.

For SOUN StockZacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Which Stock Has Better Upside Potential Now?

Both companies have credible long-term opportunities in voice AI, but they appeal to different investor styles. SoundHound offers faster top-line growth, broader end-market exposure and potentially transformative upside from the LivePerson acquisition. Cerence offers profitability, automotive leadership, cash flow strength and a deeply discounted valuation.

Given current fundamentals, Cerence appears to hold the better upside potential now. Its low valuation, improving execution, rising EPS estimates and expanding xUI pipeline provide a more balanced risk-reward profile. SoundHound remains attractive for aggressive growth investors, but its premium multiple and ongoing losses raise execution risk.

With both stocks rated Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), conservative investors may prefer Cerence today, while higher-risk investors could favor SoundHound’s longer-term AI growth story. You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.
